title: A Portrait for the Parish
premise: Estate lawyer Rosalind Brightwater is summoned to the crumbling Cornish parish of St. Merryn to read the will of Edith Penhallow, a recluse whose death certificate was filed thirty years ago. The will exists, which means someone has been legally dead and secretly alive for three decades, and among her papers Rosalind finds twin letters: one confessing to a drowning no one ever investigated, one promising an inheritance to whoever can prove who she really was. As Rosalind traces alibis woven in 1994, he discovers Edith was living under her twin sister's identity, that his own late mentor helped bury the truth, and that the parish's beloved vicar has been quietly guarding the secret, and a fortune, all along. When the vicar's accomplice turns up dead and the letters vanish, Rosalind must choose between exposing a love story that defied duty or preserving the lie, ending with him certifying the will under Edith's true name and letting the parish keep its saint while the sea keeps its secret.
about_author: Emrys Hartwell is the pen name of a former probate clerk from Falmouth who spent fifteen years reading other people's last words before writing his own. His novels are known for their fog-drenched coastal atmospheres and their fascination with the paperwork of secrets.

chapters.title: The Dead Woman's Signature
chapters.summary: Rosalind Brightwater receives a retainer to read the will of Edith Penhallow, dead thirty years on paper. In the St. Merryn registry office he finds her death certificate and, impossibly, a fresh will dated last spring. POV: Rosalind. Beat: cold professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Among Edith's effects, sealed by solicitor's order, Rosalind finds two letters in the same hand: one confessing to a drowning at Penhallow Cove in 1994, one promising everything to whoever learns her real name. The vicar, Father Callum Reeve, watches him too closely. POV: Rosalind. Beat: intrigue sharpened by the sense of being observed.

chapters.title: A Parish That Remembers
chapters.summary: Rosalind interviews villagers who speak of Edith with suspicious uniformity, as if rehearsed. The publican mentions a second sister, Morwenna, who 'went away' decades ago. Photographs show two identical girls. POV: Rosalind. Beat: the first crack in the village's careful facade.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man of 1994
chapters.summary: Archives reveal an unsolved drowning: Tobias Chenoweth, Edith's betrothed, found beneath the cliffs weeks before her recorded death. The coroner's file is missing one page. Rosalind realizes the confession letter may be literal. POV: Rosalind. Beat: dread; the mystery acquires a body.

chapters.title: What My Mentor Knew
chapters.summary: Rosalind visits retired solicitor Alistair Grebe, who drafted the original estate papers, and finds him terrified. Grebe admits he certified documents for 'Edith' after 1994 but refuses to say who walked into his office. POV: Rosalind with flashback texture. Beat: betrayal; the profession itself is complicit.

chapters.title: Morwenna's Room
chapters.summary: Breaking into the shuttered east wing of Penhallow House, Rosalind finds a room preserved since the nineties: letters between the twins, a wedding dress never worn, and a third letter addressed to him by name. POV: Rosalind. Beat: intimacy with the dead; the case becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Sermon
chapters.summary: Father Reeve preaches on Lazarus, eyes finding Rosalind in the pews. Afterward, over sherry, the vicar warns him that some resurrections cost more than they give, and reveals he wrote Edith's death certificate at her request. POV: alternating Rosalind/Reeve. Beat: the antagonist-ally emerges, sympathetic and dangerous.

chapters.title: Alibi, Thirty Years Old
chapters.summary: Rosalind reconstructs the night of the drowning: every villager's account aligns too perfectly, a wall of mutual corroboration built over decades. One fisherman's widow lets slip that Tobias was seen alive after his supposed death date. POV: Rosalind. Beat: frustration turning to methodical resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: In the churchyard, Rosalind finds an unmarked plot beside the Penhallow family stone, dug in 1994 and never opened for viewing. The sexton confesses he buried 'what the vicar gave him' at midnight. POV: Rosalind. Beat: horror; the confession letter gains weight.

chapters.title: Exhumation Denied
chapters.summary: Rosalind petitions to exhume the grave; the diocese blocks it within hours, meaning someone powerful is still protecting the arrangement. He suspects the Penhallow trustees, led by the imperious Mrs. Tresidder. POV: Rosalind. Beat: institutional obstruction; stakes widen beyond one village.

chapters.title: Letter, Interrupted
chapters.summary: The twin letters vanish from the solicitor's strongroom; the night clerk is found concussed at the harbor. Rosalind is now both investigator and suspect, and the police begin asking about his own gaps in employment years ago. POV: Rosalind. Beat: paranoia; hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: What Rosalind Buried
chapters.summary: Under pressure, Rosalind admits his own secret: as a young clerk he witnessed Grebe's irregular certification and stayed silent, trading discretion for his career. His invisibility, he realizes, was always a choice. POV: Rosalind, interior. Beat: shame and self-recognition; theme of identity turned inward.

chapters.title: The Widow's Photograph
chapters.summary: The fisherman's widow gives Rosalind a photo from 1995: 'Edith' at the harbor, but wearing Morwenna's distinctive locket, alive a year after her death. The sisters had swapped lives, but why? POV: Rosalind. Beat: breakthrough; the shape of the truth emerges.

chapters.title: Two Sisters, One Life
chapters.summary: Reconstructed through letters: Morwenna, dying of illness in 1994, begged Edith to take her name and escape a forced marriage to Tobias, whom Edith did not love. Then Tobias found out, and there was a struggle at the cove. POV: interlaced documents and Rosalind. Beat: tragic revelation; love against duty made flesh.

chapters.title: Mrs. Tresidder's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mrs. Tresidder offers Rosalind a partnership and silence: the trustees have profited from the ambiguous estate for decades. She implies she knows about his own old silence. POV: Rosalind. Beat: temptation; the corrupt offer mirrors his past sin.

chapters.title: Night at the Cove
chapters.summary: Following a light at Penhallow Cove, Rosalind finds Father Reeve standing where Tobias died, holding the stolen letters. Reeve confesses he loved Edith, helped fake her death, and has kept watch ever since, but swears he didn't take the letters from the strongroom. POV: Rosalind/Reeve. Beat: raw confrontation; grief beneath menace.

chapters.title: The Third Hand
chapters.summary: Someone else wanted the letters: the sexton's grandson, who discovered the unmarked grave's secret and was blackmailing Mrs. Tresidder. The concussed clerk identifies him. But when Rosalind confronts him, the young man is dead at the foot of the church tower. POV: Rosalind. Beat: escalation; the cover-up now has its own corpse.

chapters.title: Falling
chapters.summary: Suspicion falls on Reeve, whose alibi collapses. Rosalind, certain the vicar is guilty of concealment but not murder, races to prove it before the inquest buries the truth forever. He finds Tresidder's glove fibers on the tower rail. POV: Rosalind. Beat: urgency; moral clarity crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Confession Read Aloud
chapters.summary: At the inquest, Rosalind reads the recovered confession letter publicly: Edith's account of the struggle with Tobias, her sister's dying wish, and thirty years of penance. The room erupts; Mrs. Tresidder accuses him of forgery. POV: Rosalind. Beat: climax begins; truth as weapon.

chapters.title: Climax: The Name in the Register
chapters.summary: Confronted with the locket photograph and Grebe's final testimony, delivered from his deathbed, Mrs. Tresidder breaks and admits she helped stage the death to seize trustee control, and pushed the blackmailing boy. Reeve is cleared; the law closes in on Tresidder. POV: Rosalind. Beat: climax resolved; justice imperfect but done.

chapters.title: Certified Under Her True Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind drafts the ruling: the will stands, executed under Edith's real name, posthumously restoring her identity while shielding the parish from prosecution for its long silence. He visits Grebe, and finally forgives him, and himself. POV: Rosalind. Beat: catharsis; duty and mercy reconciled.

chapters.title: A Portrait for the Parish
chapters.summary: The parish commissions a portrait of 'Saint Edith' for the church wall; Rosalind sits for the unveiling beside Reeve, who keeps a small locket in his pocket. Walking the cliff path, Rosalind mails a letter of his own, a confession thirty years late. POV: Rosalind. Beat: bittersweet resolution; everyone remains, a little, invisible.
